chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Ash'ari, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the menstruating woman who sits out according to the number of her days—what should she do? He said: "She should wait an extra day or two, then she is a woman in istihadah; so let her perform ghusl, secure herself well, and perform every salat with wudu (ablution) so long as the blood does not pass through. فإذا نَفَذَ اغْتَسَلَتْ وَصَلَّتْ — and when it passes through, she performs ghusl and prays."

key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: she waits an extra precautionary period
key_terms.مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ: a woman in the state of istihadah (non-menstrual irregular bleeding)

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if bleeding continues after her usual menstrual days are over?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman whose habitual menstrual days have ended but bleeding continues. It explains that after waiting one or two additional days, she is treated as being in istihadah, and it outlines her duties of ghusl, taking precautions against the blood, and performing salat with wudu (ablution), with renewed ghusl when the blood passes through.
